title: Douglas Michael Mallillin confirmed as new COA chair
summary: Prior to his nomination, Mallillin was ad interim commissioner at the same agency, following a stint as deputy commissioner at the National Telecommunications Commission.

blocks.text: The Commission on Appointments holds a committee meeting on Monday, November 23, to consider the nomination of the Douglas Michael Mallillin as Commission on Audit chairperson.
MANILA, Philippines — The Committee on Appointments approved on Monday, November 23, the nomination of Douglas Michael Mallillin for Commission on Audit chairperson.
Mallillin, an outgoing ad interim commissioner at COA, will replace Gamaliel Cordoba, who was appointed associate justice on November 16.
He will complete the remaining three years of Cordoba’s seven-year term and serve as chairperson until Feb. 2, 2029.
Sen. Imee Marcos initially moved to defer Mallillin’s nomination, citing concerns about the alleged impartiality of the commission.

“The nominee, Mr. Mallillin, has served as a commissioner of COA since February 2025, and while I recognize that the commission acts as a collegial body and that not every action of the institution can automatically be attributed to an individual commissioner, his tenure nevertheless has raised legitimate questions about what steps he took to safeguard the institution against political interference and selective enforcement,” Marcos said.
Responding to Marcos’ statement, Mallillin stressed the urgency of confirming the nomination to ensure the commission’s ability to function.
The commission, Mallillin said, has had vacancy issues due to Cordoba’s appointment to the Supreme Court and Commissioner Mario Lipana’s health condition.
Marcos later withdrew her objection and allowed Mallillin’s nomination to be approved.
Prior to his time at COA, Mallillin was deputy commissioner at the National Telecommunications Commission and an assistant prosecutor for the Department of Justice.
